title: Tasks as dataclasses
description:
Model tasks with a dataclass and an enum:

```python
class Priority(Enum): HIGH = 1; NORMAL = 2; LOW = 3

@dataclass
class Task:
    title: str
    priority: Priority = Priority.NORMAL
    tags: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    done: bool = False

def parse_task(text): ...       # "Write report !high #work #urgent" -> Task("Write report", Priority.HIGH, ["work", "urgent"])
def sort_tasks(tasks): ...      # a new list: not done first, then by priority (HIGH first), then title
def with_tag(tasks, tag): ...   # the tasks that have the tag (compared ignoring case)
```

In `parse_task`, words starting with `#` are tags (stored without `#`, in lower case, in order, without duplicates); a word `!high`, `!normal` or `!low` (any case) sets the priority; everything else forms the title, words joined by single spaces. An unknown `!word` raises `ValueError`.
hints: `Priority["HIGH"]` looks a member up by name, and `Priority.__members__` holds all the names.

Tuples compare item by item (the second item only breaks a tie in the first), and `False` sorts before `True`. So `sorted(tasks, key=lambda t: (t.done, t.priority.value, t.title))` does all three orderings at once.
